sentences.ko: 이번 주말에 진짜 아무것도 안 했어. 소파에 붙어서 드라마 세 시즌 몰아보고 거의 움직이지도 않았어. 근데 이상하게 그게 딱 필요했던 것 같아.
sentences.text: I did absolutely nothing this weekend. I stayed on the couch, watched three seasons of something, and barely moved. And weirdly, that's exactly what I needed.

alts.text: Zero plans this weekend. I parked myself on the couch, binged three seasons of something, and it was the best call I made all week.
I did absolutely nothing over the weekend. I remained at home, watched a great deal of television, and hardly moved. It was precisely the rest I needed.

sentences.note: **weirdly** 는 '이상하게도'입니다. 몰아보기는 **binged**, 소파에 눌러앉는 건 **parked myself on the couch** 라고 해요.
sentences.situation: 주말에 아무것도 안 하고 쉰 게 좋았다고 말하기

sentences.ko: 배달이 잘못 왔어. 치킨 시켰는데 웬 파스타가 왔더라고. 다시 시키면 한 시간은 더 걸리니까 그냥 이거 먹으려고.
sentences.text: They sent the wrong order. I asked for the chicken and got some kind of pasta. Ordering again means another hour, so I'm just going to eat it.

alts.text: Wrong order again. I ordered chicken and they sent me pasta, and I'm not sitting here another hour waiting for a redo. So pasta it is.
The order was incorrect. I requested the chicken and received pasta instead. As placing another order would mean waiting an additional hour, I have decided to keep this one.

sentences.note: **some kind of** ~ 는 '웬 ~ 같은 것'. **pasta it is** 처럼 [명사 + it is] 는 '그럼 그걸로 하지' 하는 체념 섞인 말투예요.
sentences.situation: 배달 시켰는데 엉뚱한 게 와서 얘기하기

sentences.ko: 진짜 도와주고 싶은데 이번 주가 너무 빡세. 마감이 두 개인 데다 목요일엔 애 학교 행사도 있어. 지금 맡으면 대충 하게 될 텐데 그럼 서로 손해잖아.
sentences.text: I really want to help, but this week is brutal. I've got two deadlines and my kid's school thing on Thursday. If I said yes I'd do a rushed job, and that helps nobody.

alts.text: Man, I want to say yes. But I've got two deadlines and my kid's thing on Thursday, so I'd end up rushing it. You'd rather have it done right.
I would like to help, but this week is extremely demanding. I have two deadlines and a school event on Thursday. If I agreed, the work would be rushed and would not serve you well.

sentences.note: **brutal** 은 '살인적이다' 정도로 힘들다는 뜻이에요. **end up** -ing 은 '결국 ~하게 되다', **that helps nobody** 는 '그래 봐야 서로 손해다'입니다.

sentences.ko: 삼일 갔어. 낮에는 멀쩡한데 밤 열 시쯤 되면 냉장고 문을 열고 있더라고. 매번 똑같아.
sentences.text: I lasted three days. I was fine all day, but around ten at night I'd open the fridge and that was that. Same thing every single time.

alts.text: Three days. That's it. I'm fine until about ten, then I'm standing in front of the fridge with no memory of walking there. Every time.
I managed three days. I was perfectly fine during the day, but by around ten in the evening I would find myself at the refrigerator. It happened every time.

sentences.note: **that was that** 은 '거기서 끝이었다'는 뜻이에요. 버티는 건 **lasted**, 격식 있게는 **managed** 를 씁니다.

sentences.ko: 이사 갈 마음을 먹었다가도, 둘러보면 집도 괜찮고 월세도 괜찮고, 짐 쌀 생각을 하면 또 미루게 돼.
sentences.text: I keep almost deciding to move. Then I look around and the place is fine, the rent is fine. And I picture packing all of it, so I put it off again.

alts.text: Every couple of months I decide I'm moving. Then I remember I'd have to pack all of this, and my rent is not bad. Suddenly next year sounds great.
I have been considering a move for some time. However, my current apartment is perfectly adequate and the rent is reasonable. The prospect of packing is enough to make me postpone it.

sentences.note: **put it off** 은 미루다입니다. **I keep almost** -ing 은 '~하려다 마는 걸 반복한다', **not bad** 는 '나쁘지 않다 = 괜찮다'예요.
